answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network groups agents into a layered terrace of stake tiers and models social audits like subterranean flow across a karst terrain. For multi-agent auditing, verifiers evaluate topological cut verifications across clusters; if an audited boundary fails quorum, rogue nodes suffer complete stake slashing. Honest nodes anchor persistent trust roots beneath a cedar threshold, making attacker coordination costs scale with superlinear attacker cost.
